extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers/authors preparing submissions to EMNLP 2025 (via ACL Rolling Review)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and submission/evaluation criteria for long and short papers to EMNLP 2025, including allowable contribution types, review process (ARR two-stage), page limits, ethics/disclosure requirements, and obligations on authors (reviewing workload, presentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial, original, and unpublished research
rubrics_metrics.description: EMNLP 2025 invites the submission of long and short papers featuring substantial, original, and unpublished research on empirical methods for Natural Language Processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the primary acceptability requirement for main conference papers; submissions should present work that is both original and significant in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable contribution types
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to traditional research results, papers may contribute negative findings, survey an area, announce the creation of a new resource, argue a position, report novel linguistic insights derived using existing computational techniques, and reproduce, or fail to reproduce, previous results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMNLP explicitly encourages diverse technical contributions beyond incremental positive results; authors should frame their submission to clearly communicate the contribution type and its value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical relevance to EMNLP areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant topics for the conference include, but are not limited to, a wide range of NLP areas (e.g., Safety and Alignment in LLMs; AI/LLM Agents; Human-AI Interaction; Retrieval-Augmented LMs; Reasoning; Computational Social Science; Code Models; Interpretability; LLM Efficiency; Multimodality; MT; Multilinguality; Speech; Summarization; Syntax; Applications; Resources and Evaluation; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be relevant to one or more of the listed areas; the list is not exhaustive but indicates the conference's broad technical scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Dual submissions are not allowed! Please check the ARR Multiple Submission Policy for detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure the manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere in violation of ARR/multiple-submission policies; failure to comply can lead to rejection or other sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage review and commitment process (ARR -> EMNLP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submit articles to ARR, where submissions receive reviews and meta-reviews; authors then commit their reviewed articles to a publication venue (e.g., EMNLP 2025), where Senior Area Chairs and Program Chairs make acceptance decisions from the ARR reviews and meta-reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance decisions for EMNLP are made based on ARR reviews/meta-reviews. After a paper has been fully reviewed, authors may commit to a conference or revise and resubmit for another ARR cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship constraints during commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: During the commitment phase, it is not allowed to modify the author list (i.e., addition/deletion of authors is not allowed). However, modification of author order is possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must finalize the set of authors before commitment; any changes to authorship (adding/removing people) after ARR review are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing and anonymization
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing process will continue to be double-blind. Reviewers will not see authors, nor will authors see reviewers and reviews on ARR will not be made publicly visible. Authors will be given the option through ARR to make their anonymized submitted articles publicly visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must follow the ARR 'Instructions for Two-Way Anonymized Review' (anonymization rules). Note also: 'there is no anonymity period requirement' per ACL/ARR policies — authors can choose to make anonymized submissions public via ARR.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARR submission requirements and policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Both long and short paper submissions should follow all of the ARR submission requirements, including: Instructions for Two-Way Anonymized Review; Authorship; Citation and Comparison; Multiple Submission Policy; Resubmission Policy; and Withdrawal Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible for reading and complying with the listed ARR rules (e.g., how to cite prior work/self, resubmission constraints, withdrawal procedures). Noncompliance can affect review/acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and camera-ready allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Long Papers (8 pages) and Short Papers (4 pages). Final versions of accepted papers will be given one additional page of content (up to 9 pages for long papers, up to 5 pages for short papers) to address reviewers’ comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must adhere to the specified page limits at submission; authors may use the extra page only in the camera-ready to respond to reviewer feedback as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation requirement for inclusion in proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: All accepted papers must be presented at the conference to appear in the proceedings. The conference will include both in-person and virtual presentation options. Papers without at least one presenting author registered by the early registration deadline may be subject to desk rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one author must register (by the early registration deadline) and present (in-person or virtually) or the paper risks not appearing in the proceedings. Plan for registration and presentation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation assignment and proceedings distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Long and short papers will be presented orally or as posters as determined by the program committee. While short papers will be distinguished from long papers in the proceedings, there will be no distinction in the proceedings between papers presented orally and papers presented as posters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors cannot assume oral presentation; presentation format is assigned by program committee. The proceedings mark long vs. short papers only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reviewing workload and author-reviewer obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are expected to sign up to review, with assignments subsequently based on qualifications. The submitting authors should (a) make sure that all other authors are aware of this policy, and (b) check that everybody on their team(s) submits their (meta-)reviews on time and in accordance with the guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, all authors must complete the author registration form by May 21 2025 EoD AoE. If they get assignments, reviews must be completed by June 18, and meta-reviews - by July 15. Irresponsible reviewers may become ineligible from committing their paper(s) to EMNLP or resubmitting in the next cycle. In emergencies, contact chairs via emergency declaration form. See ACLRollingReview incentives/policies for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, disclosure, and responsible research compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must follow ACL’s Publication Ethics Policy, and ARR’s Ethics Policy including the responsible NLP research checklist, ACL’s Disclosure Policy, Limitations, and Writing Assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should complete relevant ethics checklists, disclose required information (e.g., conflicts, limitations, use of writing assistance), and adhere to responsible-research guidelines; failure to comply can affect review outcomes or lead to sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional Supplementary Materials are permitted (see Paper Submission and Templates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may include supplementary material (e.g., code, data, appendices) following ARR/EMNLP rules and templates; supplementary materials should not violate anonymization or multiple submission policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme track scope: Interdisciplinary Recontextualization of NLP
rubrics_metrics.description: The theme 'Advancing our Reach: Interdisciplinary Recontextualization of NLP' invites papers that highlight broader connections with other fields, address fundamental technology advances and evaluation methodology issues, and measure NLP's impact both within and across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theme-track submissions should engage with interdisciplinary impact and rigorous measurement of impact (distinct from standard position papers — note: 'we will not be considering position papers' for this track). Proposals that demonstrate how NLP connects to other fields or measurement strategies are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panels and Boundary-Spanning Chat proposal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel and Boundary-Spanning Chat submissions should describe the topic area and questions to be addressed, argue why the topic is strategic now (especially vis-à-vis the conference theme), describe who will participate (including short bios with specific expertise), how the session will be organized (including facilitator), and — for panels — which questions will be addressed; boundary-spanning chats should describe the proposed outcome of the session (e.g., workshop proposal, special issue, new shared task).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must justify timeliness/strategic importance, provide participant details and session structure, and specify intended outcomes; these elements will be used to evaluate panel/chat proposals.
